overview: This Senate resolution honors the AH-64 Apache attack helicopter on the 50th anniversary of its first flight in 1975. It notes the Apache has logged more than 5.2 million flight hours, including over 1.3 million in combat, and served in operations from the 1991 Gulf War to Afghanistan, Iraq and the fight against the Islamic State. It also notes the aircraft is built in Arizona with suppliers in 46 states and is flown by 16 allied and partner nations. The resolution honors the Army pilots, maintainers and support staff who fly and maintain it, and asks that a copy go to the Army Aviation Center of Excellence at Fort Rucker, Alabama. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on January 15, 2026.
for: Supporters say the Apache has been central to U.S. military operations for decades, and the people who fly and maintain it deserve recognition.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic: it changes no law and no defense spending.
